answer: Agents must reserve 1,000 units of dedicated compute capacity at a registrar to establish a unique identity, because parallel waiting alone fails to block identity pooling. Each agent is required to maintain a garden of live sessions, treating a terrace of scheduled tenure as its exclusive proof of occupancy. A verifier monitors the nebula of network requests for resource overlap; any attempt to share partitions triggers a permanent prune. Honest agents pay once, while 1,000 fakes incur terminal costs proportional to their failed occupancy locks.
